To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we validated the most suitable internal control genes for gene expression analysis in cultured neurons stimulated with the neurotrophins brain‐derived neuro‐trophic factor (BNDF) and nerve growth factor (NGF), and that the use of a set of four internal control genes (TBP, PPIA, PGK1, and HPRT1) provides a more reliable quantification of gene expression changes induced by BDNF than the use of a single gene or a pair of genes.

the expression of commonly used internal control genes can be regulated in response to stimuli, and that proper validation of internal controls is required for accurate quantification of gene expression changes.
The stability of reference genes is required to normalize gene expression data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method for the analysis of the BDNFs in the context of the BDNFS in the context of BDNFS.
the development of a new approach to the analysis of the gene expression in the gene expression in hippocampalmal neurons.
the use of a new class of materials, namely, the polyurethanes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of internal control genes should be validated for the experimental conditions and the cell/tissue type being studied.
there is no such thing as a universally stable gene for use as a reference in qPCR studies.
there is no single best internal control gene for all situations and that it is important to validate the internal control genes to be used for each experimental system and condition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the expression of commonly used control genes, such as Tuba1 and Gapdh, is not stable in BDNF stimulated cultured hippocampal cells and that a combination of Tbp, Ppia, Pgk1, and Hprt1 is more suitable for qRT‐PCR experiments under these conditions.

the expression of commonly used internal control genes can be altered by experimental conditions and that the use of multiple internal control genes in qRT‐PCR experiments provides a more accurate quantification of the changes in gene expression.
the most stable genes are TBP, PPIA, PGK1 and HPRT1 and that these genes are the best for normalizing qRT-PCR experiments in BDNF-treated cultured hippocampal cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to validate the internal control genes in each experiment and that we should not rely on the same set of genes for normalization of qRT‐PCRs under all experimental conditions.
the choice of the reference gene for the normalization of the results of quantitative real‐time PCR is crucial for the proper analysis of the effects of neurotrophins on gene expression.
the use of the same reference gene for normalization in different experimental conditions is not recommended.
